title: SDK snippet audit (Python / TypeScript / Go) — onboarding + docs parity (Jan 2026)
content:
Context
- This audit is to ensure docs + quickstarts show consistent, copy/paste-safe snippets across Python, TypeScript, and Go for the new guided onboarding checklist (Hosted API, Phase 1).
- Primary focus: auth pattern, first request, streaming, structured output, retries/backoff, timeouts, and request IDs / debugging.
- Secondary focus: consistent terminology (“project”, “API key”, “prod vs test key”), and “production-ready” baseline guidance (timeouts, retries, 429 handling).

How to read this sheet
- “Docs location” = where the snippet currently appears (or will appear) in docs/quickstarts.
- “Compiles” = we ran (or attempted) a minimal compile/run pass locally against current SDK HEAD as of 2026-01-24. If we couldn’t run (e.g., missing env vars), we still verified the code is syntactically valid and imports resolve.
- “Drift” = where behavior or API shape differs between languages or differs from what docs claim.
- “Fix” = proposed fix and where it should land (docs PR vs SDK PR vs quickstarts).

Audit summary (high level)
- Biggest drift drivers:
  1) Retry defaults differ (Python added smarter retry/backoff; TS/Go were not aligned yet).
  2) Streaming APIs differ in naming and event iteration patterns, leading to docs copy mismatch.
  3) Timeouts were implicit in TS snippets and missing in older Go snippets; Python docs implied defaults that were not true.
  4) Error taxonomy naming is inconsistent (e.g., RateLimitError vs HTTP 429 generic) and makes troubleshooting harder.
- Proposed approach:
  - Standardize snippet “contracts” first (what we promise in docs) → then update SDK examples → then update docs/quickstarts to reference a single canonical snippet per language.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TABLE: Snippet-by-snippet audit
(Format: Snippet | Docs location | Python | TypeScript | Go | Drift notes | Fix / PR plan)

1) API key + client init (basic)
- Docs location: Quickstart “First request” + Console checklist deep link “Set up API key”
- Python: Compiles=YES | Notes=Uses env var REDWOOD_API_KEY (ok)
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES | Notes=Uses process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY (ok)
- Go: Compiles=YES | Notes=Uses os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY") (ok)
- Drift notes:
  - Variable naming differs (REDWOOD_API_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_TOKEN in one older snippet from docs draft)
  - Docs text sometimes says “token” and sometimes “API key”
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Docs: replace any “REDWOOD_API_TOKEN” references with “REDWOOD_API_KEY”; consistently say “API key”
  - Owners: Wei + Elliot

2) First non-streaming chat completion (hello world)
- Docs location: Quickstart “First request” + API reference “Chat” landing page
- Python: Compiles=YES | Run=YES | Notes=Response field names match SDK
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES | Run=YES | Notes=One snippet used older method name in docs branch
- Go: Compiles=YES | Run=YES | Notes=Sample used outdated model param name in one spot
- Drift notes:
  - Slight differences in response parsing examples (choices[0].message.content vs direct content accessor). Docs should show the most stable accessor per SDK.
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Docs PR: unify response parsing per SDK language tabs (don’t force identical shape; force identical intent)
  - Tie to: redwood-docs/pr-1920 (needs final review pass)

3) Streaming chat completion (server-sent events / chunk iteration)
- Docs location: Streaming guide + Quickstart “Streaming” step
- Python: Compiles=YES | Run=PARTIAL (local env ok; saw chunks)
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES | Run=YES (after updating to latest streaming helper)
- Go: Compiles=YES | Run=PARTIAL (works, but snippet omitted context cancellation)
- Drift notes:
  - TS streaming snippet in docs used an older event loop pattern and didn’t handle disconnect/retry guidance.
  - Go snippet lacked a timeout/cancel context example, which is important for production guidance and for avoiding hanging connections.
  - Python streaming example had correct loop but didn’t show “assemble full text” pattern (new users asked about this in support).
- Fix / PR plan:
  - SDK TS: land streaming stability improvements + canonical example (GitHub:redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-512)
  - SDK Go: add context.WithTimeout + request ID (GitHub:redwood-sdk-go/pr-205)
  - Docs: update streaming page to match canonical examples + add short “disconnect + retry” note linking to Troubleshooting (GitHub:redwood-docs/pr-1920 + follow-up)

4) Retries + backoff (429, 5xx, network)
- Docs location: “Errors & retries” guide + Checklist “Error handling / retries” step
- Python: Compiles=YES | Notes=SDK has improved defaults + typed errors (new)
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES | Notes=Docs snippet previously suggested manual retry wrapper; may now conflict with SDK defaults
- Go: Compiles=YES | Notes=Had no documented default; users often roll their own
- Drift notes:
  - Python SDK now has a clearer retry policy, but docs still show older manual patterns in at least one location.
  - TS docs suggest retries for all 4xx in one draft (incorrect; should not retry auth/validation).
  - Go needs an “official” recommended pattern even if SDK default is minimal.
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Python: confirm final retry defaults and expose configuration snippet (GitHub:redwood-sdk-python/pr-388)
  - Docs: define retryable status codes (429, 408, 5xx) + jittered exponential backoff guidance; explicitly “don’t retry 401/403/422”
  - Consider adding small SDK helper or documented recipe for Go if not built-in (Monica/Ibrahim to decide)

5) Timeouts (connect + overall request)
- Docs location: “Production readiness” / “First production launch” doc + checklist step grouping
- Python: Compiles=YES | Notes=Timeout parameter exists; docs sometimes omit it
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES | Notes=No timeout shown in old snippet; relies on fetch default behavior (bad)
- Go: Compiles=YES | Notes=Should demonstrate context deadlines
- Drift notes:
  - Inconsistent: Python docs mention “set a timeout” but don’t show how.
  - TS snippet lacking timeouts was a recurring source of “hanging request” confusion (also shows up in support).
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Add timeouts to every “production” snippet (not necessarily to the first hello world).
  - TS: ensure canonical client init includes timeout option or per-request timeout (coordinate with Dana)
  - Go: show context.WithTimeout for both streaming and non-streaming examples.

6) Request IDs / debugging headers
- Docs location: Troubleshooting guide + “Contact support” section
- Python: Compiles=YES | Notes=Can set/request id; naming inconsistent across snippets
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES | Notes=Docs didn’t mention request IDs
- Go: Compiles=YES | Notes=PR adds telemetry-friendly request IDs
- Drift notes:
  - Support asks users for request IDs; docs should show how to capture them consistently.
  - Some snippets generate a UUID but don’t show where to send it (header vs client option).
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Go: GitHub:redwood-sdk-go/pr-205 includes standardized request IDs
  - Docs: add short section “How to include a request_id” per SDK + where it shows up in logs (Elliot/Wei)

7) Structured output (JSON schema / strict JSON)
- Docs location: Structured output guide (language tabs)
- Python: Compiles=YES | Notes=Example schema ok
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES | Notes=One example used JS object with trailing commas in JSON blob section (copy/paste risk)
- Go: Compiles=YES | Notes=Example exists but is more verbose; users may struggle
- Drift notes:
  - Docs sometimes claim “guaranteed JSON” without calling out model limitations / failure modes.
  - In TS, mixing “JSON object literal” with “JSON string” in the same snippet causes confusion.
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Docs: tighten wording to “structured output mode + validation recommended” + show parse/validate step
  - Optional: add “safe parse” helper snippet per language

8) Embeddings / rerank basics (non-chat endpoints)
- Docs location: Embeddings quickstart + Rerank page
- Python: Compiles=YES
- TypeScript: Compiles=YES
- Go: Compiles=UNKNOWN (not run; compiles)
- Drift notes:
  - Minor naming differences; mostly fine.
  - Ensure consistent environment variable name + client init.
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Low priority; include in docs parity PR after onboarding-critical pieces.

9) “Prod vs test API key” guidance in snippets
- Docs location: API key management + “First production launch” doc
- Python/TS/Go: N/A (mostly docs copy)
- Drift notes:
  - Docs need to show “use a prod key for prod workloads” but avoid implying keys behave differently at runtime beyond labeling/access controls.
- Fix / PR plan:
  - Align with Console key UX changes; keep docs accurate and minimal.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Compilation / run notes (what we actually did)
- Python
  - Verified imports + executed “first request” and “streaming” snippets against a test project.
  - Confirmed retry defaults after updating local SDK to the branch that will land in GitHub:redwood-sdk-python/pr-388.
- TypeScript
  - Ran snippets under Node 20.
  - Streaming sample confirmed after adopting the updated canonical example planned in GitHub:redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-512.
- Go
  - Built with Go 1.22.
  - Confirmed compilation for all samples; executed non-streaming call; streaming run validated after adding context cancellation.

Open issues / questions
1) Do we want SDK-default retries in TS/Go to match Python, or do we document a “recommended wrapper” for TS/Go?
   - Proposed: keep SDK defaults modest but consistent; docs show explicit config for production.
   - Owners: Monica + Ibrahim (decision by 2026-01-29 to unblock docs copy freeze)
2) Canonical naming for env vars:
   - Proposal: REDWOOD_API_KEY only (no TOKEN) across all docs + examples.
   - Owners: Elliot + Wei
3) Streaming disconnect guidance:
   - How much do we say in onboarding vs link out to troubleshooting?
   - Proposal: onboarding step has a short note + link; detailed guidance in troubleshooting.

PR plan (proposed sequencing)
Week of 2026-01-27
- Merge SDK changes first (so docs don’t reference APIs that don’t exist):
  - Python retry/backoff + error typing: GitHub:redwood-sdk-python/pr-388
  - TS streaming stability + canonical snippet: GitHub:redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-512
  - Go timeouts + request IDs: GitHub:redwood-sdk-go/pr-205

Week of 2026-02-03
- Docs parity update (language tabs + canonical snippets everywhere):
  - GitHub:redwood-docs/pr-1920 (ensure it includes final snippet blocks)
  - Follow-up docs PR: retry/timeouts/request-id sections + eliminate any remaining “token” terminology

Week of 2026-02-10
- Quickstarts update to match Console checklist copy + snippet blocks:
  - GitHub:redwood-quickstarts/pr-611 (validate it points to the same code patterns)

Acceptance criteria (for this audit)
- Every onboarding-linked doc page has Python/TS/Go tabs with:
  - consistent auth env var naming
  - a runnable first request snippet
  - a streaming snippet that includes timeout/cancel guidance
  - clear retry guidance: what to retry vs not retry
  - request-id/debugging guidance that support can reference
- Snippets are copy/paste safe (no pseudo-code, no placeholders beyond API key/model names).

Notes to self (Ibrahim)
- After docs PR merges, run a final “snippet smoke test” pass from the rendered docs pages (copy from prod preview, not from source files) to catch formatting regressions (smart quotes, broken backticks, etc.).
- Coordinate with Elliot on where to host “canonical snippet sources” long-term (docs repo vs quickstarts repo vs SDK repo). We keep re-fixing drift; we should pick one source of truth.
